note: The weekly loop's challenger list (owner, 2026-11-12; agents/improver.md 'The weekly loop'). One Shorts challenger runs at a time against the champion recipe. The improver starts the top entry of the right kind when a verdict lands: cycles alternate 'first-second' (judged on stayed to watch) and 'look' (judged on held after the hook); after three cycles under 45% stayed to watch the next must be 'format'. Research and the auditor add entries with evidence; the owner's recipe notes go to the top of their kind. Done entries move to `history`.

challengers.test: the hook names the subject and the price the viewer pays, then asks the viewer to guess the answer ('Costco sells you a hot dog for $1.50. Guess how much of it Costco keeps.'), against the champion's plain question
challengers.why: challenge is our best hook style (3.21x the median 48 h views, n=4) while question (0.40x, n=15) and myth (0.41x) trail; this week's breakouts hand the viewer a task: 'What Would You Buy If You Had $1 Trillion...' 1.2M at 60x its channel, 'Guess The Fake Billionaire' 27K at 141x. Keeps the champion's rule that the first sentence names the subject and figure.
challengers.note: 2026-11-15: owner note ('Please focus on script hook and topic… videos that go viral'): moved to the top of the first-second list as the hook test with the strongest evidence (challenge hooks 3.10x the median 48 h views, n=4; question hooks 0.38x, n=15). Runs as cycle 3, after cycle 1 (first-second) and cycle 2 (look) by the alternation rule.

challengers.test: rich vs poor told through two real, named people or households and one money decision (how Warren Buffett handled his kids' money against a sourced middle-class figure), against the champion's single-business story
challengers.why: 4 of 20 money Shorts at 160K+ views this week were rich-vs-poor contrasts ('How Poor vs Rich Dads Teach Their Kids About Money', 205K on 1.9K subscribers); research rates the conflict hook at 1.9x our median, and we have made none since 1 Nov

challengers.test: 15-22 s Shorts (40-60 words, 4-5 beats) against the champion's 28-35 s
challengers.why: the growing fact channel in our niche runs 15-20 s; our Shorts of 27 s or less had the best 48 h views (n=5) Research 2026-11-16: 3 of the 6 fastest-growing finance Shorts this week (market.json, 14 Nov) are under 20 s: 'How much MONEY the RICHEST streamers make' 18 s, 1.19M views (32x its channel); 'Rich vs Poor: The Harsh Reality of Society' 16 s, 930K (27x); 'The Illusion Of Money Explained In 20 Seconds' 19 s, 659K. Our own 20-24 s band is 4.56x the median 48 h views (n=3). Owner 2026-11-16: 7 of 20 money Shorts at 160K+ views this week ran 25 s or less (net-worth timelines 16-25 s at 1-1.3M); completion and loops, not length itself, are the lever.

challengers.test: every beat shows one thing filling at least half the frame, against several small things
challengers.why: the 9-10 Nov Shorts lost viewers on frames with two text buttons or small icons

challengers.test: no cast member on screen unless the story is about them: the subject and the money only
challengers.why: the cast stood beside Magic Johnson's story with no part in it

challengers.test: something new on screen every 1.5 s against 2.5 s
challengers.why: growing Shorts cut far faster than ours

challengers.test: big one-to-three-word captions in the middle (the October style) against the sentence box
challengers.why: every 1K Short in October had them

challengers.test: no text chip standing in for a thing: every label sits on a drawn or real object
challengers.why: chips like 'LIFE INSURANCE' read as a slide

challengers.test: a parable series ('same start, four people, one ends up rich') against true-fact Shorts
challengers.why: The Curious Plot's story series turns viewers into subscribers (14.5K from 36 videos)

challengers.test: the music genre picked from the story's feeling (secret and billionaire stories cinematic 88-96 BPM, how-they-make-money pop 110-116), against the seeded random genre
challengers.why: evaluator 2026-11-12: cinematic Shorts 64.1% viewed and 125% kept past the hook (n=11) against 38-43% for lofi, synthwave and acoustic; pop 2.15x the median 48 h views (n=11)

challengers.test: no beat over 6 s before the first figure lands and nothing but the hook and one short reaction or question in the first 8 s, against the champion's spine
challengers.why: v-20261024-01 followed a 3 s hook with 8.7 s of explanation and got the fewest views of its week (162); v-20261021-05 followed its hook with a 1.7 s 'Wait, what?' and is among our best (1,161 views, 73.5% viewed)
